Account.description: A provider account, by reference only (E15.1): never its secret.

config_dir.description: The harness's config dir, relative to the runner's config root (`relative_path_ok`).

credential_env.description: The variable the token goes in, one of the harness's auth variables.

credential_ref.description: The file holding the token, relative to the runner's credentials dir.

AgentAttach.description: Core to runner: write file `id` into session `session`'s folder.

name.description:
The name the user gave it; the runner derives the file's name from it
([`attachment_file_name`]), never uses it as a path.

AgentAttached.description: Runner to Core: where the file now is.

base.description: `write`: the sha-256 (lowercase hex) the file must have now; absent, the file must not exist.

path.description: `read` and `write`: a path from `valid_doc_path`, relative to the session's folder.

AgentEvents.description: Runner to Core: a session's state, and (for `agent.read`) its entries after `after`.

folder.description:
The absolute path, on the runner, of the folder the session's harness works in (its
worktree under the runner's work root, or its scratch dir there), once it has started. A
worktree is moved away when its run ends, so after the end it may no longer exist.

gateway.description:
What the session's auth gateway reported after `AgentRead::gw_after` (KAN-435). A channel
of its own, never the transcript: only the gateway task writes it.

harness_session.description: The harness's own session id, once known: what a resume continues.

plan_limit.description:
The harness's latest plan-limit event (KAN-436), a snapshot that each newer one replaces.
Sent only by a runner that lists `CAP_PLAN_LIMIT`. The agent can influence it (its tools can
forge the harness's own output), so it is a hint: cool an account from it, never disable one.

AgentFiles.description: Core to runner: the entries of `dir` of session `session`'s folder.

dir.description: Relative to the folder; empty is the folder itself.

AgentFolder.description:
Runner to Core: one level of a folder, directories first, then by name, at most
[`MAX_FOLDER_ENTRIES`].

AgentKey.description: One key of the lease: the secret lease to redeem and the host keys of the machine it logs in to.

lease.description: A secret lease (`l_...`) for the private key, redeemed by the runner, once.

pinned_keys.description:
`SHA256:<base64>` fingerprints of the host keys this key may sign for: the pins of the one
machine it logs in to. Never empty (a key with nothing pinned could sign for anyone).

user.description: The login user on that machine: a sign request for any other user is refused.

AgentLimit.description: Core to runner: set the ceiling of a live gateway session.

ceiling.description: All zero: refuse every request and abort open streams.

AgentMode.description:
A running session's new permission policy: its mode and `plan`. Its next tool calls are decided
by it at once; the harness takes it live where it can switch (Claude's `set_permission_mode`),
else at its next turn (the process is resumed with the new flags). Every later start of the
session carries it as `AgentStart::policy`.

AgentRead.description: Core to runner: the transcript after `after`.

after.description:
The last `seq` the Core holds (0 for none): entries above it are sent, those at or below
it may be dropped by the runner.

gw_after.description:
The last `gw_seq` the Core holds (0 for none): gateway reports above it are sent, those at
or below it may be dropped by the runner (KAN-435).

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for a first entry; absent or 0 answers at once.

AgentRevert.description:
Core to runner: put `path` back as it was before the session's edits. `edits` are the recorded
ones, newest first, which the runner reverse-applies (`new` back to `old`); `truncated` says a
recorded text was cut, so they cannot be reversed and the file is restored from git `HEAD`
instead. No `Debug` of the texts: they are the user's own.

AgentReverted.description: Runner to Core: the outcome of an `agent.revert`.

AgentStart.description: Core to runner: run `harness` in session `session`.

epoch.description:
Which resume this is, 0 for the first start. A session that has ended is started again
(a wake) only by a `resume` whose `epoch` is newer than the one it last ran under; the
same one again is a resent start and is answered, never run twice.

folder.description:
The session's folder in the canonical workspace (E15 §4.1, `workspace::paths::session_dir`),
set only for the built-in runner started with `--workspace-root`: the harness works there,
and the runner refuses a folder outside its workspace root (`invalid_args`). The Core checks
the runner's reported `meta.folder` against it. Absent: the runner picks its own folder.

gateway.description:
The API key the runner's gateway serves this session (KAN-435); sent only to a runner
that lists the `gateway` command. Never logged.

home.description:
A runner-bound account's home key (`CAP_BOUND_HOME`, E7-4): the harness runs with its
config dir at `<config root>/bound/<home>`, where the account's login lives. No credential
travels: the runner reads its own files.

instructions.description:
Instructions for the harness (P3-03): the approved instructions of the Brain room a
session of a project claimed. The runner hands them to the harness as a private file
beside the session, never inside the repo checkout.

live.description:
One live conversation (`CAP_LIVE`): the harness stays up after an answer and the session
is `waiting` until the next `agent.send`; it ends only on `agent.stop` or when the CLI
exits by itself. A resume (`resume`) of a live session starts no turn: it waits for the
next message, which restarts the harness with its own resume. Without it the session
ends with its first answer.

resume.description: The harness's own session to continue (`AgentEvents::harness_session`).

secrets.description: Leases the runner redeems for this session, once each. Never logged.

workspace.description: The repo and worktree to work in; absent, a scratch dir of the session's own.

AgentState.description: Where a session is, as its runner sees it.

oneOf.description:
A live session (`AgentStart::live`) whose harness finished its answer and waits for the
next `agent.send`. It still holds its slot. A runner sends it only for a live session.
Its harness ended (`outcome`).
Its harness went with a runner restart; the transcript is kept. The Core resumes it.
A state from a newer runner. Never sent.

kill.description: Kill the harness now; otherwise let its tool call in flight finish, then end it.

turn.description:
Only a live session's running answer is stopped (like Esc in the CLI): the session goes
on, `waiting`. A runner that lists `CAP_LIVE` honours it; the Core sends it to no other.
Nothing happens when no answer runs. Overrides `kill`.

AgentSubagentStop.description:
Stops the sub-agent a session's harness started with the tool call `tool_use_id` (Claude Code's
`Task`/`Agent`, by its `stop_task` control request); the turn goes on, and that call ends with
its result. A harness that cannot stop one sub-agent ignores it (the Core sends it for none).

AgentWrite.description:
Core to runner: write `content` to `path` of session `session`'s folder (parent folders are
created inside it). No `Debug` of the text.

AgentWritten.description: Runner to Core: the file was written.

Arch.description: A CPU architecture, as Rust names it (`std::env::consts::ARCH`).

CacheInfo.description: One warm project cache on a runner.

tree_hash.description: The tree the cache holds now (`TreeHash`).

CallUsage.description: The tokens a `gateway.call` used, as the upstream reported them.

battery.description: Absent on a host with no battery.

caches.description: The warm project caches this runner holds (§4.5).

cpu_pct.description: CPU use, 0 to 100, averaged over 60 s.

disk_free_mb.description: Free disk under the runner's cache root.

gate.description: The runner's own verdict on taking jobs (E15-4 `hwgate`).

idle_secs.description: Seconds since the last user input on the host (This Mac); absent where unknown.

job_slots.description: How many jobs it runs at once: default `cores / 4`, at least 1.

mem_free_mb.description: Memory available to new work ("available", not "free").

toolchains.description: Toolchains ready for jobs, `rust`, `node`, `python`, `go`, `xcode`, `swift`, `docker` to version.

Captured.description: One output pipe: redacted UTF-8 (lossy), cut at the limit with a marker.

bytes.description: How many bytes the process wrote, kept or not.

truncated.description: `text` was cut at the limit and ends in `TRUNCATED_MARKER`.

Ceiling.description: What a session may spend through the gateway; `agent.limit` changes it while it runs.

Close.description: A stream given up. From the Core on a running command: cancel it.

Command.description: Core to runner, the first frame of a command stream.

oneOf.description: Answers `result` at once: proves the path end to end.
A TCP stream to an exposed port of a live run (P6-01); bytes are `output` frames.
Session documents (E10-2): list, read or write the `.md` files of a session's folder.
(After every older op.) Wait for a runner-bound sign-in to finish (E7-4).
(After every older op.) Wipe a removed runner-bound account's home (E7 closeout).
E12-4 (after every older op: the schema-compat gate tells variants by position).
An op from a newer Core: answered `unsupported_command`. Never sent.

ConnTool.description: One tool the harness may see.

description.description: What it does and the arguments it takes, for the model.

input_schema.description:
The JSON Schema (an object schema) of its arguments, for the harness's tool list. Absent
from an older Core: the runner then lists an open object.

oneOf.description: Runner to Core, the first frame of a connection, on stream 0.
Core to runner: the hello is accepted.
Core to runner: the Core's half of the connection proof (`auth`).
Runner to Core: the runner's half of the connection proof (`auth`).
Core to runner: a planned identity key rotation (`auth`).
Runner to Core, the first frame on a `pty.open` or `pty.attach` stream (`terminal`).
Core to runner on a terminal stream: the client's new size.
Core to runner on a terminal stream: deliver a signal to its process group.
Runner to Core on a terminal stream: the screen now; output resumes at its `seq`.
Core to runner on an `ssh.sftp.write` stream: the last byte was sent (`sftp`).
Runner to Core on a `sync.watch` stream: what changed in the session folder (E15-2).
A type from a newer peer: ignored. Never sent.

CoreAuth.description: Core to runner, the answer to `hello`.

core_spki.description: The Core identity SPKI (91 bytes), base64url.

sig.description: ES256, raw r‖s, base64url: the Core key over `core_auth_message`.

boot.description:
The Core process's random id (E1-11.4): another than last time means the Core
restarted, and every stream the runner held is gone.

heartbeat_ms.description: Between heartbeats, each way; silent for three is a dead connection.

protocol.description: The version the Core speaks on this connection.

streams.description:
Every command stream the Core still has in flight for this runner, with how many runner
frames it received on each: the runner resends the rest. A stream the runner holds that
is not listed is over for the Core (answered, or reported lost).

Credit.description: Flow control: the sender of this frame accepts `bytes` more `output` bytes on the stream.

DesignBox.description: One node's absolute box, in points.

DesignCheck.description: `design.check`: is this upload a font, or an Icon Composer `.icon` zip, the helper can use?

DesignChecked.description: The answer to `design.check`: `ok`, or a fixed sentence why not.

DesignExport.description:
`design.export` (V6-03): one screen as an inert HTML/CSS package. The answer carries the page and
its stylesheet; the fonts and images it names are the job's own files, which the caller already
holds, so they are not sent back.

fallback_font.description: The hash of one of `fonts` that `system` text falls back to (plan Q2: Linux has no SF Pro).

screen.description:
A resolved id of a top-level node of the page; absent, the page's first screen. `doc.theme`
is only the theme the page opens in: the package carries both.

DesignExported.description:
The answer to `design.export`. Files of the package: `index.html`, `style.css`, and for each
hash in `fonts` / `images` the file `fonts/<sha256>` / `assets/<sha256>` (the job's bytes).

metrics_differ.description: Some text used a font other than the library file it names (plan Q2).

screen.description: The resolved id of the screen exported (what `design.render`'s `node` takes).

width.description: The screen's size in points, as the engine lays it out: the viewport a shot of it needs.

DesignFidelity.description:
`design.fidelity`: how far two PNGs of one screen are apart (the engine's frame, Chromium's shot
of the export). Both are decoded only in the helper's sandbox.

DesignFidelityScore.description:
The answer to `design.fidelity`: the share of pixels that differ by more than the tolerance
(CIE76 delta E), in percent. Sizes that differ are a score of 100.

DesignFile.description: A file by its library hash: `sha256` (lowercase hex) and its bytes, standard base64.

DesignFinding.description: A geometry finding: `rule` (`geometry.outside`, `geometry.text_overflow`), the node, a sentence.

metrics_differ.description: Some text used a font other than the library file it names (plan Q2: "metrics differ").

fallback_font.description: The hash of one of `fonts` that `system` text falls back to (plan Q2: Linux has no SF Pro).

DesignRender.description: `design.render`: one screen or node (or the whole page) as a PNG, CPU Skia.

fallback_font.description: The hash of one of `fonts` that `system` text falls back to (plan Q2: Linux has no SF Pro).

node.description: A resolved node id; absent, every screen of the page.

DesignReview.description: `design.review`: geometry findings (what needs real text metrics and layout).

fallback_font.description: The hash of one of `fonts` that `system` text falls back to (plan Q2: Linux has no SF Pro).

DesignShot.description:
`design.shot`: headless Chromium opens `entry` of `files` (an HTML export or a mockup package)
with no network and screenshots the viewport.

DesignShotFile.description: One file of a `design.shot` site: a relative path (no `..`, no leading `/`, no NUL or `\`).

DiskReport.description: A runner's disk use (1.15, E15.9), as measured after its last clean-up pass.

caches_bytes.description: The shared build caches, one per repo (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, package stores, …).

full.description: Over the cap with nothing left it may evict.

mirrors_bytes.description: The bare repo mirrors, which hold every issue's branch: never evicted.

removed.description: Issues whose worktrees this pass removed: idle past the limit, or evicted for room.

worktrees.description: Each worktree it holds, oldest use first.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex sha-256 of the bytes.

DocsReply.description: Runner to Core. `list` fills `files`; `read` fills `text` and `sha256`; `write` fills `sha256` (the new one).

DriverInfo.description: A driver a runner offers (`exec`, `agent`; `pty` later).

capacity.description:
How many of its commands run at once; one more is answered `busy`. For `agent`: how
many sessions.

commands.description: The command ops it takes, e.g. `noop`, `exec.run`.

slots.description:
Per kind within the driver (`agent`: per harness), how many run at once; together at
most `capacity`. Empty: no split.

streams.description:
How many of its commands may be in flight at once, when that is not `capacity` (a
driver whose work outlives its commands, like `agent`): the hub counts these per
driver. Absent: `capacity`, counted with every other driver's.

Egress.description:
Destinations a session may (`allow`) or may not (`deny`) reach, as IP literals or CIDR
blocks. Host names are refused: they are the runner operator's, resolved only by the
egress proxy outside the sandbox. A session's rules can only narrow what the runner allows.

Entry.description: One file of a tree. Directories are implied by their files.

chunks.description: Each [`CHUNK_BYTES`] chunk's hash, in order; empty for an empty file or a symlink.

oneOf.description: A relative symlink that resolves inside the project; `Entry::link` is its target.
A kind from a newer peer: skipped. Never sent.

ErrorCode.description: Machine codes, snake_case like the client API's (handshake spec §14).

oneOf.description: A frame or payload that does not parse, or a stream id that breaks the rules.
The peer's protocol major is not one this side speaks.
No advertised driver takes this command op.
The command's arguments are refused (e.g. a relative `cwd`).
The driver is at its advertised capacity; retry later.
The program could not be started.
The command was cancelled by a `close`.
Anything else on the runner's side.
The connection proof failed (`auth`); the same answer whatever the reason.
The Core's identity is not the one the runner pinned. Logged by the runner; never sent.
The runner is not connected (Core side, to whoever dispatched).

The connection went while the command was in flight and its outcome is unknown: it may
or may not have run. Reported once per command, never followed by a result.

`ssh.exec`: the host presented a key the Core has not pinned (none pinned yet). Nothing was
authenticated; `host_key` has the fingerprint for a person to trust.
`ssh.exec`: the host presented a key other than the pinned ones. Nothing was authenticated.
`ssh.exec`: the host refused the key (or it could not be read).
`ssh.exec`: no connection, no common algorithm, or the channel failed.
`ssh.sftp.*`: no such path on the host.
`ssh.sftp.*`: the host refused the user access to the path.
`ssh.sftp.*`: the path is taken (a write without `overwrite`, a rename, a mkdir).
`ssh.sftp.*`: the host refused for another reason, or the SFTP session failed.
A transfer over `SFTP_MAX_BYTES`.

`design.*`: the helper (or Chromium) failed, crashed, or was stopped at a limit; `message` says
which. The input is what it could not handle; the runner itself is unaffected.

`design.*`: the helper (or Chromium) ran out of wall clock. Load on the runner can cause it as
much as the input, so it is no verdict on the file: try again later.
`sync.*`: a chunk or file did not hash as listed, or the tree after a push is not `want_tree`.
`sync.push`: the cache is not at `base`.

`sync.*`, `job.run`: a path that is not a wire path (`wire_path_problem`), or one outside
the project.
`job.run`: the job's sync out is over `MAX_SYNC_OUT_BYTES`.

`pty.open` to a runner that no longer opens terminals (E15-4): only the Core and This Mac
do.
A code from a newer peer. Never sent.

ExecLimits.description:
What the Core asks for; the runner clamps each to its own ceiling and uses its default
for an absent one.

max_output_bytes.description: The most of stdout, and of stderr, kept; the rest is dropped and marked.

timeout_ms.description: Wall clock until the process group gets TERM, then KILL.

exit_code.description: Absent when it was ended by a signal (its timeout included).

timed_out.description: It ran past its timeout and was killed.

ExecRun.description: Runs `program args…` to its end, bounded, and answers with its exit and output.

cwd.description: An absolute directory; absent, the runner's own working directory.

env.description: Variables set in the child as given.

env_pass.description:
Names of the runner's own variables to pass on. Only those also on the runner's
allow-list are; the child's environment starts empty.

payload.description:
The body for `kind` (`Body`; schema `V2Payload`); absent for `heartbeat` when its payload
is the default `Heartbeat`.

oneOf.description: A kind from a newer peer: skipped. Never sent.

Gate.description: Whether a runner takes jobs now, by its own measure. The Core's pause always wins over `Open`.

oneOf.description: The host is in use (This Mac: not idle and CPU at or above 30%).
Paused on the host itself.
Takes no jobs at all (no `job` driver, or switched off). Also what an absent gate reads as.
A gate from a newer runner: read as not open. Never sent.

GatewayAuth.description: The header the gateway puts the key in.

oneOf.description: `x-api-key: <key>`
`Authorization: Bearer <key>`
`x-goog-api-key: <key>`

GatewayCall.description:
Core to runner (E15-0): redeem `lease`, run the same dial checks as `gateway.test`, make one
`POST` of `body` to `path` under the upstream's base path, and return the response. No `Debug`.

body.description: The JSON request body, as text (already redacted by the Core).

path.description: The request path under the upstream's base path, e.g. `/v1beta/models/x:generateContent`.

upstream.description: Absent reads as no upstream, which the runner refuses (`invalid_args`).

GatewayCalled.description:
Runner to Core: the answer to `gateway.call`. `body` is the upstream's response text, at most
[`MAX_GATEWAY_CALL_BYTES`] (longer is `truncated`), only for a status of `ok`.

http_status.description: The HTTP status, 0 when none came back.

retry_after.description: Seconds the upstream asked to wait, for an overload.

GatewayGrant.description:
Core to runner, in `AgentStart`: the key of one account, served to the harness by the runner's
gateway. `lease` is redeemed into the gateway's memory, never the env or a file. No `Debug`.

account.description: The account id, for the runner's logs; the ledger takes it from the Core's own row.

models.description: The model ids the session may name.

prices.description: The list price of each model in `models`, for the per-request reservation.

provider.description:
The account's provider id (`anthropic`, or a user definition's id): the runner runs
[`key_host_problem`] with it before dialing. Absent reads as empty, which no key passes.

user_key.description: The user definition's key shape and host, for a user-defined provider.

GatewayReport.description:
Runner to Core, in [`AgentEvents::gateway`](super::AgentEvents): what the gateway saw. It has
its own channel and its own `gw_seq` (per session, from 1, by one), acknowledged by
[`AgentRead::gw_after`](super::AgentRead), and only the gateway task writes it: nothing the
harness prints can become one. It names no account and no model the Core did not allow; the
Core takes the account from its own session row.

approximate.description: The counts are the gateway's estimate: the stream was cut, dropped or never reported usage.

cache_read.description: Input tokens read from a cache.

cache_write.description: Input tokens written to a cache.

epoch.description:
The `epoch` of the start the report was made under (`AgentStart::epoch`), set by the runner
when it numbers the report. The ledger's key is session, epoch and `gw_seq`.

input.description: Input tokens not served from a cache.

model.description: The model the request named (checked against the grant), for a usage report.

reported_usd_micros.description:
What the provider itself reported as the cost, when a response header the gateway parsed
said so. Absent otherwise.

reset_at.description: When the upstream's limit resets, as it said (an RFC 3339 time), for an upstream report.

retry_after.description: Seconds the upstream asked to wait (`retry-after`), for an upstream report.

status.description: The outcome class of the request.

oneOf.description: One request's tokens: the ledger records it.
An upstream signal (rate limit, auth failure, ...): no tokens.
A kind from a newer runner. Never sent.

GatewayTest.description: Core to runner: redeem `lease`, run the dial checks, make one free request.

test_path.description:
The path of the one request, under the upstream's base path, when the provider's own model
list is not an authenticated call (OpenRouter lists models without a key, so a revoked key
would read as `ok`). Absent: the wire's own model list, which every built-in provider
authenticates.

GatewayTested.description:
Runner to Core: the status class and latency of a [`GatewayTest`], and the model ids it asked
for; never any other part of a body.

models.description:
The model ids the provider listed, when [`GatewayTest::want_models`] asked and the list was
read in full: ids only (bounded), never any other part of the body. Provider text: the
Core filters each id before it keeps one.

Hash.description: A blake3 hash, lowercase hex on the wire (64 characters).

Heartbeat.description:
A runner's heartbeat: carries `load` when the runner measured one, and the isolation it
offers now.

capacity.description: Its capacity now (E15-1). Absent from a runner that predates 2.1.

isolation.description:
The isolation the runner offers now (E8a-09): a change shows in the next heartbeat, so a
tier that goes away is no longer offered by the Core's next placement. Absent from a
runner that does not report it, and from one that offers no agent driver.

load.description: The host's load when the heartbeat was sent; absent when the runner has no measure.

report.description: Its tool install, home folder and last error. Absent from a runner that predates it.

HistoryChunk.description:
Runner to Core: the new parts, the cursor after them (only sessions that moved), what was
skipped, and whether more waits.

HistoryItem.description: One part of one session: the text said in its entries `first` to `last`.

path.description: Where it came from, relative to the harness's history folder.

project.description: The working folder the session ran in, as the harness recorded it.

text.description: `User: ...` and `Assistant: ...` blocks, redacted by the runner.

HistoryRead.description: Core to runner: the new entries of `harness`'s sessions after `cursor`.

cursor.description: Per session id, the last entry (line) already taken.

harness.description: The harness whose history to read: `claude` (the others are not readable yet).

max_bytes.description: The most text the answer may carry, up to [`MAX_HISTORY_BYTES`].

HistorySkip.description: What was not read, and why (`restricted_path`, `unreadable`, `no_time`).

HostKeyEvidence.description: Which hop of an `ssh.exec` a host-key refusal is about, and the key it presented.

HostLoad.description:
The host's load when a heartbeat was sent (1.26): its one-minute load average and its CPU
count. The server stretches a loaded runner's lease by `avg1 / cores`, up to a cap.

HostLoad2.description:
The host's load when a heartbeat was sent (E2-15.2): its one-minute load average and its
CPU count, so the hub can apply load-based back-pressure and report it through the API.

cores.description: How many CPUs the runner sees.

InlineFile.description: A small file's bytes, carried in its event.

Isolation.description: How strongly a session is isolated from its host, weakest to strongest.

oneOf.description: The harness runs as the runner's user (the default of a runner with no sandbox).
A process sandbox: bubblewrap or Seatbelt.
A virtual machine with its own kernel.

IsolationCaps.description:
What isolation a runner can give right now (E8a-09). Placement is by this, and the runner
checks again when a session starts; a stale or forged advertisement therefore never gets a
session a weaker sandbox than it asked for.

tiers.description:
Every tier offered now, by name (`Isolation::as_str`). A runner whose probe fails stops
listing the tier. Names, not the enum, so a tier from a newer runner parses here and
simply meets nothing.

JobDone.description: Runner to Core: the answer to `job.run`.

changed.description: Every file the job changed or created, as it is now: the Core pulls them (§4.6).

exit_code.description: Absent when a signal ended it.

tree.description: The cache's tree after the job.

JobNeed.description: What a job needs of the hardware it runs on.

toolchains.description: Toolchain names (`Capacity::toolchains` keys) it needs, reported or installable from pins.

xcode.description: Needs Xcode: a macOS runner that reports `xcode`.

JobRun.description: Core to runner: run `argv` in `cwd_rel` of the cache (or workspace) of `project`.

cache.description:
The cache the job runs in: `<work_root>/cache/<core_id>/<project_id>/`, named by the runner
from `project`; this is the Core id part. Empty on the built-in runner (the workspace).

cwd_rel.description: A wire path, relative to the cache root; empty is the root.

env.description: The child's environment, which otherwise starts empty.

hosts.description:
The hosts the job may reach, already within [`JOB_REGISTRY_HOSTS`] (the asking session's
own `filtered` list cut to it, E15 H2). Absent: the whole registry list. The runner cuts it
to the registry list again.

origin.description:
Who asked: `s:<session>`, `t:<terminal>` or `u` (a person or a task), set by the Core. A
job from another origin than the last one's finds the cache's home and build folders
cleared (E15 M5).

prepare.description: Run first, in the same folder (`npm ci` when the lockfile changed). Empty: nothing.

secrets.description:
Single-use leases, redeemed into the env, never written to disk; their values are redacted
from the output.

Kvm.description: The state of `/dev/kvm` on a runner, for the microvm tier (E8a-09).

oneOf.description: No VM tier is built into this runner, or the host has no KVM concept (macOS).
The host has no `/dev/kvm`.
`/dev/kvm` is there and the probe passed.
`/dev/kvm` is there and the probe failed (permissions, a broken host).
A state from a newer runner: read as not usable. Never sent.

LogLine.description: One line of a service's output, redacted and cut to [`LOG_LINE_MAX`].

at.description: When the container wrote it (RFC 3339, from Podman).

seq.description: Grows by one per line of the run, across services; the resume cursor.

Login.description:
A login place on a runner host (1.20): `dir` is relative to its config root
(`claude`, `accounts/claude-a`), or `credentials/<file>` for an account's token file.

harness.description: The harness, when the dir is a harness's own.

state.description: `logged_in`, `logged_out`, or `unknown` (the login lives in the keychain).

LoginCancel.description: Core to runner: stop the sign-in and wipe what it made.

LoginCode.description: Core to runner: the approval code the user pasted.

LoginInput.description:
Core to runner: one line the user typed into a guided sign-in (a pasted code, or a menu choice),
sent with Enter. A secret: no `Debug` that shows it, never stored, never logged.

LoginResult.description:
Runner to Core, the answer to `login.code` and `login.cancel`: the token (once; the runner
zeroizes its copy) or an error, never both.

done.description: A runner-bound sign-in finished: the credential is in the account's home on the runner.

LoginScreen.description:
Runner to Core, the answer to `login.screen`: what the CLI shows, after the redactor and cut to
the last lines. Text only; nothing but a typed line ever goes back.

code.description: A device code the CLI printed, if any.

url.description: The sign-in page the CLI printed, if any.

LoginScreenReq.description: Core to runner: the current screen of the sign-in.

LoginStart.description: Core to runner: begin the sign-in of `harness` (`claude`).

home.description:
A runner-bound sign-in (E7-4/5/5b): the key of the account home the runner logs in to
(`[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`, a dir of the runner's own). The credential never leaves it. Absent
is the Claude sign-in, whose token comes back once.

LoginUrl.description: Runner to Core, the answer to `login.start`: where the user signs in.

code.description:
The one-time device code the user types on that page (Codex). Not a credential: it is
shown to the user and is useless once the sign-in ends.

LoginWait.description:
Core to runner: wait for the runner-bound sign-in `login_id` to finish; answered by a
`login.result` with `done` set, or an error. No code is typed and no token comes back.

LoginWipe.description:
Core to runner: delete the home of a removed runner-bound account. The runner checks the key
(`bound_key_ok`), touches only `<agents-config>/bound/<home>`, refuses a symlink there, and answers
a `login.result` with `done` set (also when there was nothing to delete), or an error. An
Antigravity home's login also lives in the OS keyring, which cannot be cleared per account: the
answer is then `done` with `error = "keyring_not_cleared"` (the home is gone; the Core records the note).

ModelPrice.description:
The list price of one model, in micro-dollars per million tokens, for the gateway's
per-request reservation (decision: the Core's price book, carried in the grant).

Os.description: An operating system, as Rust names it (`std::env::consts::OS`).

Outcome.description: How a run ended, as its runner saw it.

oneOf.description: `fingerprint` is the error class + step, for the loop breaker.
Usage reached the run's token cap.
No progress for `RunLimits.stall_after_secs` (1.14): the runner stopped it.

Output.description: Bytes on a stream (exec output later, terminal `out`/`in`), standard base64.

oneOf.description: Everything outside the allowlist asks.
File edits inside the run's directory go ahead; the rest asks.
The harness acts without asking. Only with `sandboxed`.

PlanCheck.description:
Core to runner: redeem `lease` (a subscription token, env), run `claude -p` with a one-word
prompt in the sandbox, and answer what happened.

PlanChecked.description: Runner to Core: how the check ended. Never the CLI's text.

plan_limit.description:
The plan windows Claude reported on the check's answer (its `rate_limit_event`), stored on
the account like a session's. Absent from an older runner or when Claude said none.

PlanLimit.description: The latest plan-limit event of a session, overwritten by each newer one (no sequence number).

PlanWindow.description: One plan window, e.g. Claude's `five_hour` and `seven_day`.

resets_at.description: When the window resets, in seconds since the epoch.

utilization.description: A fraction of the window's limit: 0.0 to 1.0, and past it at the limit.

PodmanFacts.description: Podman as the runner finds it.

rootless.description: The rootless setup for the `ainkrad-run` user is complete (user, subuid/subgid, linger).

Policy.description: A project's harness permission policy (1.3). Never full-auto by default.

allow.description:
Tools the harness may use without asking: a tool name (`Edit`, `fileChange`), or
`<tool>:<command prefix>` (`Bash:cargo test`) for a command with no shell operators, or a
chain of commands each of which it covers.

disk_mb.description: Disk cap in MiB, 16 to 1048576. It can only lower the runner's own cap.

effort.description:
How hard the harness thinks: `low`, `medium`, `high` or `max` (Claude's `--effort`, Codex's
`model_reasoning_effort`). Absent: the harness's own default. Only a runner that lists
`CAP_EFFORT` takes it; an older runner refuses the field.

egress.description: Destinations the session may reach, narrowing the runner's own allowlist.

image.description: The guest image, by digest (`sha256:` + 64 hex). Only a tier that boots an image takes it.

memory_mb.description: Memory cap in MiB, 64 to 262144. It can only lower the runner's own cap.

min_isolation.description:
The weakest isolation the session may run in (E8a-08). Absent: any runner. A runner that
cannot offer it is never given the session, and refuses it if it is (E8a-09).

plan.description:
Plan mode: the harness reads and plans and edits nothing (Claude Code's `plan`). Only a
harness that has one takes it; an older runner refuses the field.

sandboxed.description: Runs must work in a disposable sandbox: only a sandboxed runner may take them.

vcpus.description: Virtual CPUs, 1 to 32. Only a VM tier has them.

wall_secs.description: A hard wall-clock cap in seconds, 1 to 86400: the host kills the sandbox at the deadline.

workspace.description: How the workspace reaches the sandbox. Absent: `bind`.

PolicyApplied.description: The answer to `runner.policy`: the policy was saved and the runner is restarting.

restarting.description: The runner restarts a moment after this answer; it reconnects with the new policy.

PortClosed.description: Why a port stream ended, as its last frame.

reason.description: `eof` (the service closed it) or `run_ended` (the run stopped, failed or lost the port).

PortOpen.description: Opens a stream to `port` (the container port, as written in the spec) of `service` in run `run`.

project.description: The project the run belongs to; the runner refuses a run of another project.

PtyAttach.description: `pty.attach`: reach a running terminal and resume its output at `seq`.

seq.description: The next output byte the attacher wants; older than the runner keeps gets a snapshot.

watch.description: Only watches for the exit (the Core's monitor), not a client; see [`PtyOpen::watch`].

PtyClose.description: `pty.close`: hang the terminal up (HUP, then TERM, then KILL) and answer its exit.

PtyOpen.description: `pty.open`: a login shell, or `program args…`, in a new PTY.

cwd.description: An absolute directory; absent, the user's home.

env.description: Set in the child as given.

env_pass.description: Names of the runner's own variables to pass on; only those on its allow-list are.

purpose.description:
Why the terminal is opened (E15-4). Kept for the wire only: no purpose makes a remote
runner open a terminal (E15 security review M7; the Accounts sign-in is `login.start`).

sandbox.description:
Where the shell lives (D-17): `home`, `project:<id>`, `session:<id>` or `real`; see
[`SandboxMode`]. Absent: the runner-wide sandbox of before this field (an older Core), a
`real` shell. Needs `sandbox_user` unless `real`.

sandbox_user.description: The Core user whose persistent sandbox home the shell gets (`[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}`).

scrollback_budget.description:
The runner's total scrollback disk budget (E2-06.2), applied by LRU across its
terminals; the runner clamps it. Absent: unchanged.

scrollback_bytes.description:
The disk cap for this terminal's scrollback; the runner clamps it to its bounds.
Absent: the runner's default.

session.description:
The AI session (`as_…`) whose folder `cwd` is, set only by the Core when a client opens a
terminal for a session. The runner starts the shell only when `cwd` is the folder it
recorded for that session (else `invalid_args`), and its terminal sandbox then lets the
shell reach that one folder although it lies in the runner's hidden state.

ssh.description:
An interactive SSH terminal (Leyline): the runner starts its own `ssh-pty` as the terminal's
program, handing it the redeemed keys over an inherited pipe. Then `program`, `args`,
`cwd`, `session`, `env` and `env_pass` must be empty (`invalid_args`).

watch.description:
This stream only watches for the exit (the Core's monitor): it is not a client, so it
does not protect the terminal's scrollback from the disk budget.

PtyTail.description: `pty.tail`: the last `lines` (1 to 20) non-empty rows of the terminal's screen, as plain text.

expose.description: The spec marked it `expose: true`: the only ports `port.open` serves (P6-01).

host_port.description: Where it listens on the runner's 127.0.0.1.

Rate.description: How fast a session may call.

Reply.description: Runner to Core, a command's last frame when it ran.

oneOf.description: A terminal's exit, on the stream of the op that saw it.
Every `agent.*` op answers with the session's state (`agent.read` with its entries).
The answer to `login.start`.
The answer to `login.code` and `login.cancel`.
(After every older op, as `Command`'s.) The answer to `agent.tools`: the calls the harness made.
The answer to `runner.policy`.
The answer to `tools.install` and `tools.status`.
The answer to `plan.check`.
The answer to `history.read`.
The answer to `ssh.exec`.
`run.start` and `run.stop` answer with the run's state; `run.status` with every run asked for.
`run.observe`: service metrics and the new log lines of one run.
The last frame of `port.open`.
The answer to `agent.docs`.
The answer to `login.screen`.
The answer to `runner.update` (E12-4).
An op from a newer runner. Never sent.

RepoDiff.description: One repo's worktree against its base (1.18): `git diff --numstat` plus untracked files.

insertions.description: Lines added (an untracked text file's every line) and removed.

repo.description: The repo's name in its project; empty for an issue's only repo.

RevertEdit.description: One recorded edit of a file: the text it took out and the text it put in.

oneOf.description: The recorded edits were reversed in the file.
The file was created by the session: it is deleted.
The file was restored from git `HEAD` (edits that cannot be reversed).
The file no longer holds the recorded text; nothing was changed.
Nothing can revert it (no usable edits, and not tracked in git); nothing was changed.
A result from a newer runner. Never sent.

Rotation.description: Core to runner: move the pin from `old_fp` to `new_fp`.

not_before.description: Unix seconds from which the Core may present the new key.

seq.description: Increases with every rotation; a runner applies only a higher one.

sig.description: ES256 by the old key over `rotation_message`, base64url.

Route.description: One entry of an agent's fallback chain (E15.3), with the account picked for it.

RunCaps.description: What a project run may count on (see [`RunnerFacts::run_caps`]).

can_clone.description:
Can clone a project repo from the Core's copies (agent driver on): a spec that builds
from or mounts repos is placed on such a runner first (P5-05).

isolate.description: Project networks can be isolated from each other (`--opt isolate=true`).

mem_mb.description: Memory of the host in MB.

RunCheckout.description:
A repo checkout of this run. With `from_core` the runner clones it itself, from the Core's copy
(P3-02's clone for AI sessions, which the Core leased to this runner for the run), and `dir`
is empty: the runner picks the directory. Without it `dir` is a checkout the runner already holds.

dir.description: Absolute path of the checkout on the runner host.

RunClone.description: Where a run's checkout is cloned from (P5-05).

mirror.description: The project repo id: the Core serves its copy to this runner only while it holds a lease.

remote.description: The repo's remote: the checkout's `origin` (no credentials, as `repo_url_problem` checks).

cmd.description: Run in the container by its shell; exit 0 is healthy.

failed_service.description: With `failed`: the service that is not running.

RunLimits.description: What the runner is told of the server's settings for one run (1.11, E15.17).

approval_timeout_secs.description: How long an escalated tool call waits for a reviewer before it is denied.

fallback_on_model_unavailable.description:
Whether a turn failing for this class moves the run to the next entry of its fallback
chain (1.20); otherwise the run fails. Absent from an older server: it does.

max_resumes.description: Resumes of a dropped session before the run gives up on its model (E15.4).

resume_backoff_ms.description: The first wait before a resume, doubling per drop, and the longest.

stall_after_secs.description:
How long the run may go without progress before it is stopped as stalled (1.14,
E15.7). Absent from an older server: `STALL_AFTER_SECS`.

tool_output_bytes.description:
The most of a tool's output a `tool_result` transcript event carries (1.18). Absent
from an older server: `TOOL_OUTPUT_BYTES`.

warm_max.description:
Idle harness servers the runner keeps for later runs (1.13, E15.6); 0, none. Absent
from an older server: none.

RunLimits2.description: The project's caps, applied to every container of the run.

lost.description: Lines between `after` and the oldest line held that the ring had already dropped.

after.description: Lines with a `seq` above this (0: from the oldest the runner still holds).

health.description:
The caller is an admin route: the runner may run the services' health checks (`podman
healthcheck run`) for this run. Without it, health is only what Podman last recorded.

limit.description: At most this many lines (default and most [`OBSERVE_LINES_MAX`]).

oneOf.description: No container of the run is left.
A service is not running (`failed_service`).

port.description: The container port; published on the runner's loopback only, at a port Podman picks.

RunSecret.description: A secret the spec names, as a lease (`l_…`) the runner redeems once.

env.description: Plain values, or values with `${secret:NAME}` that the runner fills from `RunStart::secrets`.

volumes.description: Volume name to the container path it is mounted at; the volume is `ainkrad-p<project>-<name>`.

RunSpec.description: A project's run spec: its services by name (P4-01's `RunSpec`, as JSON).

RunStart.description:
Starts run `run` of project `project`: network, volumes, checkouts, builds, then the services
in `depends_on` order. Answers `run.start` with the run's [`RunInfo`].

RunStatusReq.description: One run's state, or (no `run`) every run on the runner, read from container labels.

RunStop.description: Stops a run: `podman stop -t 10`, then its containers are removed; volumes stay.

RunToken.description:
A run token on the wire. Its `Debug` is redacted, so logging a message never logs it;
`expose` is the one way to read it.

RunnerFacts.description:
Facts a runner reports about itself in its hello (display only: the Core decides nothing by
them).

os_pretty.description: The system as a person names it, `Ubuntu 26.04` or `macOS 15.1`.

own_logins.description:
Harnesses that hold a login of their own on this host (`claude`, `codex`, ...): the Core
cannot see it, so a plain session of one of these is not refused as `no_account`.

podman.description: Podman on this host, when it is installed. Absent from a runner that predates project runs.

policy.description:
What the runner offers now (terminals, agents, agent capacity). Absent from a runner
that predates the runner policy.

run_caps.description:
What project runs can use here. Present only when every prerequisite holds (Podman, the
`ainkrad-run` user with subuid/subgid and linger, cpu/memory/pids delegated): a Core must
not place a run on a runner without it, because the limits would be silently ignored.

tool_install.description: The runner's own report (latest heartbeat): see [`RunnerReport`].

tools.description:
Tools found on this host, name to version (`claude` to `2.1.318`, `git`, `node`, `python`,
`go`, `rust`, `docker`, `codex`), probed at every connection.

user.description: The user the runner process runs as.

boot.description:
The runner process's random id (E1-11.4). The same `boot` as the last connection means
its streams survived and are resumed; another means they are gone (reported `lost`).

capacity.description:
Its capacity when the hello was sent (E15-1), beside `load`. Absent from a runner that
predates 2.1: the Core then treats it as plain session hardware ("update runner").

device_id.description:
The runner device, `d_…`: the one that signed the upgrade (E1-11.3). The Core refuses a
hello without it.

drivers.description: What it can run. The Core sends only commands listed here.

facts.description:
What the host and the runner process are, for the App's runner page. Absent from a runner
that does not report it.

isolation.description:
The isolation the runner offers (E8a-09), beside `arch`. Absent from a runner that does
not report it: the Core then treats it as offering no guarantee, and places no session on
it that needs one.

load.description:
The host's load when the hello was sent (E2-15.2): the one-minute average and CPU count,
so the hub can apply load-based back-pressure before any heartbeat.

nonce.description: `nonce_r`, 32 random bytes, base64url (`auth`). The Core refuses a hello without it.

protocol.description: `PROTOCOL_VERSION` of the runner; the Core refuses a major it does not speak.

streams.description:
Every command stream the runner still holds, with how many Core frames it received on
each: the Core resends the rest.

terminals.description:
Every terminal this runner's host processes hold (E2-03), so a Core that lost its
streams (a runner or Core restart) can `pty.attach` again.

RunnerInfo.description: What a runner says of itself (1.20).

logins.description:
Each harness and account config dir (and account token file) it found, and whether it
is logged in there.

power_nap.description: The Power Nap preference it holds, as the server last sent it.

slept_secs.description: How long its machine last slept, if it slept since the daemon started.

RunnerLimits.description:
What the runner is told of the server's settings for it (1.15, E15.9, decision #57: server-wide
per runner, not per company).

disk_cap_bytes.description: The most its work root may hold: worktrees, shared build caches and repo mirrors.

disk_evict_percent.description: Share of the cap past which idle worktrees are evicted, oldest first, then caches.

warm_idle_secs.description: How long a warm harness server may sit idle before it is stopped (E15.6).

workspace_idle_secs.description:
How long a worktree may sit with no run before it is removed (its work kept on its
branch, uncommitted changes on `refs/citadel/wip/<issue>`), recreated on demand.

RunnerPolicy.description:
What a runner offers. The same shape is the command, the answer and the runner's report of
what is active (`RunnerFacts::policy`).

agent_capacity.description: How many agent sessions run at once, 1 to [`MAX_AGENT_CAPACITY`].

runs.description:
The runner takes project runs (`run.start`). Off by default; the Core places runs only on
runners that have it on. An older policy without it reads as off.

share_history.description:
The runner answers `history.read` (the Brain reads its Claude Code history): `--share-history`.
Off by default; an older Core's policy without it reads as off.

RunnerProof.description: Runner to Core, once it has checked `CoreAuth`.

sig.description: ES256, raw r‖s, base64url: the runner's routine key over `runner_auth_message`.

RunnerReport.description:
What a runner says about itself in every heartbeat, beyond load: its AI tool install, its
sandbox home folder and the plain-words reason it is not fully working. The Core keeps it
beside the hello's facts and serves it with `GET /runners`.

home.description: The folder the runner's work happens in.

install.description: The install under way or the last one; absent when none ran since the runner started.

last_error.description: The runner's last-error note (why it is up without AI tools), cleared when it starts them.

RunnerUpdate.description:
Core to runner (E12-4): the Core saw a newer signed runner and this one is idle, so update. `version` is only what the
Core expects (a plain version, checked for shape); the runner's root-side updater reads the signed manifest itself,
installs only a newer signed release, restarts the runner and rolls back if it does not stay up. A Mac runner updates
with the app and answers `unsupported_command`.

RunnerUpdateAccepted.description:
The answer to `runner.update`: the request was handed to the updater; the runner restarts a moment later and
reconnects on the new version.

SecretGrant.description: One secret for a session: its lease, and the variable it is delivered under.

lease.description: `l_…`, redeemable once, by this runner only.

var.description:
The environment variable: the value itself (`env`), the file's path (`file`), or the
askpass helper's path (`askpass`, also set as `GIT_ASKPASS`). `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`.

ServiceHealth.description: A service's own health check, when its spec has one.

oneOf.description: No health check.

cpu_percent.description:
Percent of one CPU (it passes 100 with more than one core in use); `None` while it is not
running or Podman gave no sample.

memory_limit_bytes.description: The cap Podman reports (the project's memory limit); 0 when unknown.

SftpEntry.description: What the host said about one path. Every field is the host's word, so data.

name.description: The entry's name in a listing; the path as asked for `stat`.

SftpList.description: `ssh.sftp.list`: the entries of a directory, sorted by name, without `.` and `..`.

SftpRead.description: `ssh.sftp.read`: a file's bytes as `output` frames, from `offset`.

SftpRemove.description: `ssh.sftp.remove`: a file or symlink, or with `dir` an empty directory. Never recursive.

SftpStat.description: `ssh.sftp.stat`: one path's attributes. A symlink is reported as a symlink unless `follow`.

SftpTransferred.description: The answer to `ssh.sftp.read` and `ssh.sftp.write`: the bytes moved.

SftpWrite.description: `ssh.sftp.write`: a file from the Core's `output` frames, ended by `control` `eof`.

mode.description:
Permission bits (`0o7777`) set on the file before any byte is written, so a file meant for
its owner alone (Leyline's runner invite, `0o600`) is never readable by anyone else.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (`sftp_exists` when absent and the path is taken).

size.description:
The size the sender will send: over the cap is refused at once, and a different count at
`eof` fails the transfer (nothing is left behind).

SignalReq.description: `control` `signal`: deliver one of [`SIGNALS`] to the terminal's process group.

Size.description: A terminal's size in cells; `control` `resize` carries one.

Snapshot.description:
`control` `snapshot`: the visible screen as bytes a terminal view replays (standard
base64), after which output resumes at `seq`.

SshAgentDrop.description:
Ends the agent `id`: the listener and every connection close and the keys are wiped, before the
answer. Dropping an id that is not live (ended, never loaded) is not an error.

SshAgentDropped.description: What the agent did before it ended.

refused.description: Sign requests refused (unbound session, unpinned host, expired, wrong data).

was_live.description: The agent was live when the drop arrived (not already over).

SshAgentLoad.description:
Starts an agent on the runner under `id` (the Core's name for it): the keys are redeemed, a socket
opens in a 0700 directory of the runner's own temporary directory, and the agent answers
`SshAgentLoaded`. It ends at `ttl_secs`, on `ssh.agent.drop`, or when the runner has been cut off
from the Core for 5 minutes.

SshAgentLoaded.description: Where the agent listens, for the person's `ssh`.

config.description:
An `ssh_config` beside the socket: `IdentityAgent`, a private `UserKnownHostsFile`, public-key
authentication only, no agent forwarding. `ssh -F <config> ...` is the whole ready command.

SshExec.description:
Runs `run` on `target`, through `hops` (jump hosts, first to last), and answers with the exit and
output of the remote command: an `ExecResult` with `exec.run`'s limits, redaction and capacity.

run.description: The command line, given to the remote user's shell as the SSH `exec` request.

SshHop.description: One machine on the path: where, as whom, which host keys are trusted, and which key to prove with.

lease.description: A secret lease (`l_…`) for this hop's private key, redeemed by the runner, once.

pinned_keys.description:
Host keys the Core trusts for this machine, as `SHA256:<base64>` fingerprints (what
`ssh-keygen -l` prints). A presented key not listed here ends the connection before any
authentication: `host_key_unknown` when this list is empty, `host_key_changed` when not.

SshTerminal.description:
The machine an interactive SSH terminal (`PtyOpen::ssh`) reaches, through `hops` (first to last):
the same hops, pins and key leases as `ssh.exec`, and the same rules (at most `MAX_SSH_HOPS`).
The runner redeems the leases and passes the keys to `ssh-pty`; a password or keyboard-interactive
prompt is answered by the person typing in the terminal.

StreamError.description: A command's failure, or (on stream 0) a connection's. `message` is human text, redacted.

host_key.description: With `host_key_unknown` and `host_key_changed`: whose key, and which.

StreamState.description:
Resume by `seq` (E1-11.4): how many of the peer's frames one side received on a stream.
Frames are numbered from 0, so this is also the next `seq` it expects.

SyncDrop.description: Core to runner: forget the cache of `project` (it was archived, or the session ended).

SyncDropped.description: Runner to Core: the answer to `sync.drop`.

SyncEvent.description:
Runner to Core on a `sync.watch` stream (a `control` body `sync_event`), at most every
[`WATCH_INTERVAL_MS`] while something changed. A `put` entry with no `inline` is pulled.

SyncManifest.description: Core to runner: the manifest of the runner's cache of `project`.

lease.description: `l_…`: the per (device, project, job or session) lease; without it, `not_found`.

rules.description: The rules the manifest is taken under.

rules_hash.description: The hash of `rules` (a runner may keep its index per rules hash).

seed.description:
F0-bis (E15-4): seed an empty cache with `git clone` from the Core's copy of the project's
repo before the manifest is taken (spec §4.4). The Core serves the copy only while it holds a
lease for this runner. Absent: the cache is not seeded (or already is).

SyncManifestReply.description: Runner to Core: the answer to `sync.manifest`.

SyncPull.description:
Core to runner: send these files' chunks (credited `output` frames), from a cache or a session
folder.

cache_or_session.description: The project's cache (empty) or an overflow session's id (`as_…`).

paths.description: `(wire path, the hash the Core expects)`; a file that no longer hashes so is `hash_mismatch`.

SyncPulled.description: Runner to Core: the answer to `sync.pull`, after the last chunk.

SyncPush.description:
Core to runner: apply a delta to the cache, then the chunk frames of `put`. Refused with
`base_mismatch` when the cache is not at `base`, `hash_mismatch` for a chunk or file that does
not hash as listed, `path_refused` for a path that is not a wire path.

base_files.description:
A per-file base, for a person's write into an overflow session (§4.6): each `(path, the
hash the Core last saw)`. When present the push conflicts only where one of these files
changed (`base_mismatch`), and `base` is not checked. Empty: the whole-tree `base`.

session.description:
The overflow session (`as_…`) whose live folder the push writes, as `sync.watch` names it.
Absent: the project's cache, or the session the lease's watch registered (older Cores).

want_tree.description: The tree the cache must hold afterwards; another is `hash_mismatch`.

SyncPushed.description: Runner to Core: the answer to `sync.push`.

SyncRules.description:
The project's include/exclude rules (§4.4, the built-ins merged with `.ainkrad/jobs.toml
[sync]` by the Core). Globs are gitignore-style, relative to the project root. `.git/` is
excluded whatever these say.

exclude.description: Never synced in (build output, secret-shaped files).

include.description: Synced although an exclude matches (secret-shaped files the project lists, for one).

outputs.description: Synced out after a job even inside an excluded dir (`target/release/app`).

SyncWatch.description: Core to runner: stream every change in an overflow session's folder until `close`.

rules.description: The rules the watched tree is taken under.

SyncWatched.description: Runner to Core: the last frame of `sync.watch` (after `close`).

TerminalExit.description: How a terminal's child ended: the `result` of every `pty.*` op.

exit_code.description: Absent when it was ended by a signal.

host_key.description:
An interactive SSH terminal that never reached a shell because a hop's host key was not
trusted (exit code `SSH_PTY_EXIT_HOST_KEY_UNKNOWN` or `_CHANGED`): which hop, and the key it
presented. Reported by `ssh-pty` itself over a private descriptor, never read from the
terminal's output, which a remote shell controls.

signal.description: The signal's description, when one ended it.

TerminalInfo.description:
A terminal as its runner sees it: `control` `opened`, and each entry of
`RunnerHello::terminals`.

seq.description: Output bytes so far: the next byte's offset.

TerminalState.description: A terminal's lifecycle (E2-01.1): created → running → exited → reaped.

oneOf.description: Asked for; the child is not running yet.
The child ended (it is waited for); its exit is not read yet.
A client read the exit: the host is gone and the id is free.
A state from a newer peer.

TerminalTail.description: The answer to [`PtyTail`]: rows oldest first, each at most 400 characters.

TokenCaps.description:
A run's caps, split (1.27): what the runner counts its tokens against. A run stops when
either applies. Its tokens are counted from its events, and the caps stay exact for the
budgets and the issue; only `run` is weighted.

cache_weight_divisor.description: How much a cache token counts against `run`, as a divisor (1: every token in full).

exact.description:
The least left in the budgets and the issue's cap that apply, counted in full (0 is
stop at once); absent when none applies.

run.description:
`run.token_cap`, compared with the run's tokens where cache reads and writes count at
`1 / cache_weight_divisor` (0 is stop at once).

Tokens.description: Token counts. A cap counts their `sum`.

cost_usd_micros.description:
What the harness itself says the run has cost so far, in millionths of a US dollar,
when it says (Claude's `total_cost_usd`, OpenCode's session cost; 1.6). Not part of
`sum`. Absent: the server prices the tokens, or leaves them unpriced.

Tool.description:
A tool the runner host can install. A fixed list: the runner and its root helper refuse any
other name.

ToolBatch.description: Runner to Core: the calls after `ToolsPoll::after`.

ToolCall.description: Runner to Core: the harness called `tool`.

id.description: Made by the runner; the result names it.

tc_seq.description: Per session, from 1, by one: the Core's cursor over it.

ToolInstallReport.description: How an AI tool install on a runner stands (D-22): the one under way, or the last one.

step.description: What it is doing, a short sentence: `Downloading Claude 2.1.318`.

ToolResult.description: Core to runner: how call `id` ended. Either `result`, or a plain `code` and a fixed `message`.

approval.description:
`ainkrad.call` only: the request id (`cm_…`) of the person's approval the call waited for,
whatever its answer (E6.5: a script's result says which calls were approved or denied).

ToolsInstall.description:
Core to runner: install `tool`. `operation` is the Core's id for the operation (`tools.status`
names it); not `op`, which is the command's tag on the wire.

after.description: The last `tc_seq` the Core holds (0 for none).

tools.description: The whole tool list now; absent: unchanged. An empty list takes every tool away.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for a first call; absent or 0 answers at once.

step.description: What it is doing, a short sentence: `Downloading Node 22.22.1`.

tools.description: When `done`: the tools the runner found on its host after the install (what `RunnerFacts::tools` holds).

ToolsStatusReq.description: Core to runner: how is operation `op`?

TranscriptEntry.description: One transcript entry: redacted by the runner before it is kept.

body.description: The harness event, or the driver's own (`approval_request`, `gap`, `ended`, …).

TreeHash.description: The hash of a whole tree: blake3 over its sorted entries (E15-2 defines the exact fold).

Upstream.description: Where the gateway dials: from the account row's frozen `base_url`, never from the agent.

base_path.description: The path the wire's routes hang under (`""`, or `/v1` for the OpenAI wire).

host.description: The host name, no scheme, port or trailing dot (443 only).

UpstreamStatus.description: The outcome class of an upstream request or test: a status class only, never provider text.

oneOf.description: A class from a newer runner. Never sent.

UserKeyDef.description:
A user-defined provider's key shape and frozen host: what the runner needs to run
[`key_host_problem`] as the broker did. Absent for a built-in provider.

V2Payload.description: A v2 Frame's payload by kind: control Control, command Command, result Reply, error StreamError, output Output, credit Credit, close Close, heartbeat Heartbeat.

Wire.description: The upstream API dialects the gateway speaks: a closed set, so the route table is code.

Workspace.description: Where an issue's run works: a git worktree of `repo` on `branch`, cut from `base`.

also.description: The issue's other repos, in its project's order, when it touches several (1.16).

expected_head.description:
The sha the branch was last pushed at (1.28), `None` before its first push. The runner
leases its push on it, so a rewritten branch lands only over the head it last saw.

mirror.description:
A project repo (P3-02): clone it from the Core's copy of that repo id, not from `repo`
(which stays its remote, for the checkout's `origin`). Only the Core sets it, for a session
of a project; the Core serves the copy to this runner only while it holds a lease for it.

name.description: The repo's name in its project (1.16): its worktree's directory in a multi-repo workspace.

push.description:
Push the branch to the repo's origin when the run ends (1.7): its project is on a forge,
where a PR is opened from it (E9.1).

repo.description: A URL or path git can clone, never holding credentials (`repo_url_problem`).

WorkspaceMode.description: How the session's workspace reaches the sandbox.

oneOf.description: The worktree is bound into the sandbox (every process tier).
The worktree is copied in and the result copied out; no host path is shared (a VM).

active.description: A run is using it: never evicted.

idle_secs.description: Seconds since a run last used it.

description: RunnerMessage: runner to server (v1). ServerMessage: server to runner (v1). Frame: either way (v2, multiplexed streams).

oneOf.description: Runner → server.
The first message of every connection.

disk.description: Its last disk report (1.15), if it made one.

harnesses.description:
Installed harness → version, e.g. `claude` → `2.1.306`, from its `--version` (or
`unknown (…)` when unreadable). A version at or above the adapter's minimum and not
known bad gets work (1.21); a refused one marks the runner unhealthy (E3.6).

info.description: Its state (1.20); absent from an older runner.

os.description: Its operating system and CPU architecture (1.25), e.g. `macos` and `aarch64`.

runs.description: Runs it is still working on, to resume after a reconnect.

oneOf.description: The answer to `Probe` `request` (1.25): what it found now.

error.description: Why it could not look, if it could not.

oneOf.description: Its state, after each clean-up pass (1.20).

The answer to `ReadLog` `request` (1.20): the last lines of its log, redacted, or why
not.
Its disk use after a clean-up pass (1.15, E15.9).

It has a free slot and wants one run. `workspaces`: the issues it holds a worktree
for (1.1).
It is still working on `run`; `load` (1.26) is the host's load when it says.

`run` progressed (1.14): a tool call, a file change, a new message or more tokens.
`diff_files`: how many files its worktree differs from the base in, when measured.

repos.description:
Each repo's diff against its base, in the issue's repo order (1.18); empty when not
measured.

oneOf.description: The harness for `run` is up; `session` is its resumable session id, if it has one.

One transcript chunk, numbered from 1 per run, redacted (`redact`). The server stores
each `seq` once; a resend is ignored.

The run's token totals so far, numbered from 1 per run (1.2). Totals, not deltas: a
lost or repeated report loses or double-counts nothing.

The harness asks for a tool call the run's policy does not allow (1.3). `id` is the
harness's request id, unique within the run; `input` is redacted. Resent after a
reconnect until answered; the server keeps one approval per `(run, id)`.
The run moved to the next entry of its fallback chain (1.9): `harness` and `model` as
in the `Assign`'s `fallbacks`, working as `account`; `class` is why (`model_unavailable`,
`rate_limited`, `quota`, `no_account`), `reason` the harness's words, redacted.

The provider dropped the run's turn and the runner resumes its session (1.10). Not
resent: a drop lost to a dropped connection is not counted.

timeout_secs.description:
How long the runner waits before denying it (1.5), so the server expires the
approval at the same moment. Absent from an older runner: the server's deadline.

oneOf.description:
The answer to `ReadFile` `request` (1.17): the file's bytes in standard base64, or why
it was not read.
Server → runner.

limits.description: Its disk and warm-process settings (1.15); absent, the runner's defaults.

power_nap.description: The admin's Power Nap preference for it (1.20); absent, none set.

oneOf.description: A claimed run for the runner to start. Holds no secret.

account.description: The provider account to work as (1.8); absent, the runner's own harness login.

context_ref.description: Where the run's context is read, through the Citadel MCP server (E4.2).

fallbacks.description: The rest of the agent's fallback chain, in order (1.9).

instructions.description:
The run's skills rendered as markdown, for the harness's instructions file (1.4,
E4.3); absent when the run has none.

issue_key.description: The issue's key, e.g. `CIT-12`, for the prompt (1.4).

limits.description: The run's limits from the server's settings (1.11); absent, the runner's defaults.

policy.description: The project's permission policy (1.3); absent, the default (ask).

prompt.description:
The run's first turn (1.22): its job on this wake and its done rule; absent, the
runner's own.

resume_session.description:
A session of the run's harness to continue rather than starting a new one (1.12,
E15.5); absent, a fresh session.

token_cap.description:
Tokens the run may use: the least left in any budget that applies, or the
server's default (1.2). Absent from an older server: the runner's default.

token_caps.description:
The run's caps split (1.27), see `TokenCaps`; absent from an older server, which
sends `token_cap` alone.

workspace.description: The issue's git worktree, when its project has a repo (1.1).

oneOf.description:
The started run's token, for the harness to call back with. Sent once per start or
re-start (a resumed `RunStarted` rotates it).

Stop and forget `run`: it was cancelled, ended already, or this runner no longer holds
it. Send no `RunEnded`.
`RunEnded` for `run` was recorded.

The answer to `ApprovalRequest` `id` of `run` (1.3): `reply` is the reviewer's note,
which a denial passes to the agent as its reason.
Finish the tool call in flight, then stop `run`'s turn and end it `Cancelled` (1.19).
The admin's message `id` for `run`'s harness, given to it as its next turn (1.19).
Remove the worktrees of these issues: they are done, cancelled or gone (1.1).

Read `path`, relative to `run`'s worktree, of at most `max_bytes` (1.17); answered by
`FileRead`.
The last `lines` lines of the runner's own log (1.20); answered by `LogTail`.
The admin changed its Power Nap preference (1.20).
Look at yourself again now (1.25); answered by `Probed`.
`run`'s permission policy changed (1.24): its next tool calls are decided by `policy`.
A message was refused for a reason other than the run: a protocol or storage error.
